items.title: John Best interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: Helen Forrest — she was in the band with Billie.

ctx.x: Did she have to come in through the kitchen door sometimes? That kind of thing?

Oh that part, you’re talking about the Lincoln Hotel in New York. I mean that’s where that — the bandstand at the Lincoln Hotel was facing the audience and the ballroom floor. To the right was a door to the kitchen at the other end of the bandstand. And all the tables and stuff were out in front. And the other entranceway, that was the Lincoln Hotel, and we had to come through the kitchen. Otherwise you’re walking right down through the — and we were used to that. I don’t know exactly what happened there, but…

Right, okay. I wanted to ask you something, you were taking about listening to Louis Armstrong, and that you considered those records to be older stuff, that you had to go back and listen to. But this was late 1930s you were talking about, right? And Louis had recorded those records only about ten years before that. Is that right? So it really wasn’t that big a space between the time when you had to go back and listen to him, it was only ten years, is that right? So really it kind of wasn’t that old.
